book_title: 0. Executive Thesis, Dual Verdict & Opportunity Matrix
question: After re-auditing MPS Limited's fundamentals and updating live prices through late November 2026, why do we downgrade new capital to REJECTED despite a debt-free 38.7% ROCE franchise trading below 19x trailing earnings?

epigraph.quote: Underwriting Rule: grade the business first and the tape second, because a great balance sheet still hurts when bought inside a Stage 4 breakdown.
epigraph.author: Portfolio Desk Charter

web_blocks.html: What MPS does and what changed in November 2026. MPS Limited (NSE: MPSLTD; BSE: 532440) builds journals, school and medical courses, and corporate training for global publishers and health systems [1, 2]. It runs three units: Research Solutions (~58% of Q2 FY27 sales; 48.17% EBITDA margin), Education Solutions (~31%, including Unbound Medicine), and Corporate Learning (~11%, freshly turning positive at 24.74% Q2 margin) [1, 2, 103, 104, 105]. Cash stood at ₹163.23 Cr on 30 September 2026 with zero bank debt. Ten-year operating cash flow matches profit, and management raised the FY27 EBITDA floor to ₹310 Cr [1, 2, 106]. Yet our blind Pass 1 audit found four real cracks. Organic Education ex-Unbound fell −9.9% YoY in Q2 (−23.3% organic EBITDA) [104]. Unbound's royalty model caps margins near 18% while facing free clinical-AI leader OpenEvidence (703,265 U.S. doctors), which just signed a deal with Unbound licensor Johns Hopkins Medicine [99, 100, 102]. Research ex-AJE staff also jumped +20.42% ahead of billing, and the ADI BPO merger carries a merchant-banker due-diligence disclaimer [103, 107]. At the same time, the stock broke into Stage 4. It fell from ₹2,105.60 on the 23 November 2026 NSE ledger to ₹2,054.80 on the 25 November 2026 live TradingView close (−2.41% on 1.47x 30-day volume), breaking its 200-day average (₹2,084.67) and pivot S1 (₹2,065.93) [90, 91].
The decision matrix below pulls together both session prices, refreshed fair values, business-quality status, and zero-allocation risk controls.

web_blocks.takeaway: We still respect MPS's debt-free cash flow, yet Pass 1's Compounder Pass is strictly provisional and we reject new capital today. A 31% drop into Stage 4 leaves just +6.0% to +8.6% base weighted upside (+2.3% to +4.8% under Severe-Bear stress to ₹1,336) and sub-12% M&A-adjusted IRR.

web_blocks.html: Why we stay on the sidelines—and what brings MPS back. Stage 4 peers eClerx (−34.9% 1Y, 19.1x P/E) and Newgen (−53.5% 1Y, 18.5x P/E) show that AI fear does not stop at 19x earnings [91]. Wolters Kluwer's 2026 buyback price fell 47% even as organic profit grew [65, 89]. Short-term (1–3 months) is AVOID / REJECTED. Medium-term (6–18 months) is REJECTED / MONITOR ONLY. Long-term (3–5 years) stays a CONDITIONAL WATCHLIST. Two keys must turn together before we re-open this file. First, price must form a Stage 1 base and close weekly above the 30-week average (₹2,293) on at least 2x volume. Second, H2 FY27 results must prove at least ₹156 Cr EBITDA, Research margins of 45% or higher as new billing scales revenue per head, positive organic Education growth, and clean ADI BPO / CARO tax resolution.

book_paragraphs: This companion refresh asks a sharper question than our November 12 monograph: when a high-ROCE, debt-free compounder finally falls to your old support price—but slices straight through the 200-day moving average on heavy volume just as fresh cracks appear in its Education and clinical-AI divisions—do you buy the dip, or do you step aside?

Our answer is clear and unsentimental. We downgrade MPS Limited for new capital to REJECTED with zero allocation. Our Zerodha account holds zero shares, so nothing is sold. Pass 1's Compounder Pass is explicitly provisional: ten-year cash flow, ₹163 crore of debt-free cash, 48 per cent Research margins, and Corporate Learning's Q2 turnaround are offset by a 37 per cent FY26 drop in tangible net worth (to ₹102.2 crore, with goodwill and intangibles at 52.5 per cent of assets), zero dividend yield, −9.9 per cent Q2 organic Education contraction, OpenEvidence's alliance with Unbound licensor Johns Hopkins Medicine, a 20.4 per cent ex-AJE Research hiring jump, ₹36.3 crore of unreconciled CARO tax disputes, and a merchant-banker due-diligence disclaimer on the ADI BPO merger.

Putting those discoveries into a fresh valuation cuts our Base 12-month value from ₹2,410 to ₹2,275 and lifts our Bear weight to 30 per cent at ₹1,593 (with an RWS-style Severe-Bear stress floor at ₹1,336, −35 to −37 per cent). Even at ₹2,105.60 (23 Nov ledger) and ₹2,054.80 (25 Nov live TV), base probability-weighted upside is just 6.0 to 8.6 per cent—dropping to 2.3 to 4.8 per cent under Severe-Bear stress—while deducting ₹64.5 crore of annual historical M&A spend cuts implied ten-year IRR below our 13 per cent hurdle to 11.6–11.7 per cent.

We keep 100 per cent of reviewed marginal cash safely in our ₹14.21 lakh Zerodha cash reserve and wait for two simultaneous proofs: a real Stage 1 base followed by a high-volume Stage 2 reclaim above the 30-week average near ₹2,293, paired with second-half proof that organic Education stabilizes, Research hiring converts into higher billing per employee, and ADI BPO / CARO tax questions close cleanly.

book_callouts.title: PROLOGUE BRIEFING: WHY PRIOR WAIT-FOR-SUPPORT BECAME REJECTED
book_callouts.quote: When the floor gives way and fresh business risks appear, cancel the old watch rather than catching the knife.
book_callouts.text: Between 12 November and 25 November 2026, both the chart and our Pass 1 forensic audit shifted against deploying capital.
bullets: Tape breakdown: 25 November close of ₹2,054.80 broke the 200-day average (₹2,085) and pivot S1 (₹2,066) on 1.47x volume, confirming Stage 4 (−10.4% under 30W SMA).
Pass 1 bruises: Organic Education contracted −9.9% YoY in Q2 (−23.3% EBITDA), OpenEvidence (703k MAUs) partnered with Johns Hopkins Medicine, and Research ex-AJE headcount jumped +20.4%.
Valuation reset: Refreshed Base value ₹2,275 and weighted ₹2,231 leave only +6.0% to +8.6% upside against −22.5% to −24.4% Bear risk (₹1,593).
Discipline: Zero shares held, zero capital deployed, and passive ₹1,810–₹1,920 / ₹1,750 reference markers strictly monitor-only.

book_subsections.title: Reading both session dates and the path back to consideration
paragraphs: Throughout this refreshed monograph we cite both the verified 23 November 2026 NSE ledger close (₹2,105.60) and the 25 November 2026 live TradingView print (₹2,054.80) without ever blending the two. The two-day gap matters because 23 November was the final session MPS clung above its 200-day moving average before breaking cleanly into Stage 4 on 25 November.

Nothing in this rejection writes off MPS forever. If second-half FY27 filings confirm the ₹310 crore EBITDA floor, stabilize organic Education, prove Research AI leverage, and close the ADI BPO merger without hidden tax liabilities—and if institutional volume drives a Stage 2 reclaim above ₹2,293—this desk will gladly re-open the file.
